title: Add traceable expense allocation batches for multi-customer containers
description: Extend the existing container expense preview and generation workflow so allocations to multi-customer container participants have explicit batch and source lineage. Reuse the existing allocation methods and FinanceExpense records rather than creating a second accounting engine. Do not infer missing bases, post payments, settle receivables or payables, rewrite legacy allocations, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: The existing expense-allocation workflow can preview allocation of one eligible source expense across active participants of one Container Loading List using the supported volume, weight, carton, amount or documented whole-container method.

Every participant basis used by a preview comes from an explicit persisted value or user-confirmed request value validated by the server; missing or zero total evidence is rejected rather than guessed.

Preview is read-only and returns participant, method, basis, ratio and allocated amount, with deterministic currency-precision rounding and any remainder assigned by a documented stable rule so line totals equal the source amount.

Generation records an allocation batch identifier plus source expense, container/loading-list reference, participant Customer, method, basis, ratio and allocated amount for every generated allocation row.

A successful batch is generated transactionally; partial rows are not retained when validation or persistence fails, and duplicate active generation for the same source expense and allocation scope is rejected.

Corrections preserve history through an explicit voided batch state rather than hard deletion; voiding does not silently alter the original source expense or create payment, receipt or accounting postings.
Legacy allocated expense rows without batch lineage remain readable and are clearly identified as legacy/untracked; no automatic backfill is performed during normal requests.
Allocation does not change Container Loading detail quantities, participant identity, Trade Documents, inventory, Purchase Orders, Sales Orders or authoritative shipment tracking.

Repository schema changes are idempotent and validated only through permitted local or test-database paths; production database execution and irreversible finance operations remain behind human gates.

Unit/integration tests cover every supported basis, rounding remainder, zero or missing bases, duplicate generation, transactional rollback, void history, legacy allocations and non-mutation of source records; safe validation passes.
Browser/UI acceptance is recorded as deferred during development according to project policy.

scenarios: Open an eligible container expense, preview allocation across two persisted container participants, and verify bases, ratios, rounding and allocated totals before generating one traceable batch.
Attempt duplicate generation, then void the generated batch and verify lineage remains visible while the source expense, container quantities and unrelated finance records remain unchanged.

human_gate.reason: Repository allocation logic and non-production test schema only. Production database execution, real financial settlement, irreversible operations, deployment and release are not authorized.
